CSE - Execute Script (Basic).vi

Owning Palette: CSE Advanced VIs

The VI executes a parsed CSE Script with additional functionality. The VI takes a reference to CSE instance context returned by CSE - Parse Script.vi and uses this reference to access a parsed script and keep intermediate data. The VI is reentrant, instances of the VI can simultaneously execute parsed scripts.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

VC Handle has to contain a handle of variable context in order to make it possible to operate on variables in a script. Use VM - Open Context.vi to open a variable context
CSE RefNum is a reference number for a CSE instance that contains a parsed CSE script. CSE - Parse Script.vi returns a value that can be wired directly to this terminal.
Stm Index specifies an index of the statement in the parsed script that should be executed, or from which execution should either start or continue. It has to be zero when you start script execution. Then, if you run the VI in a debugging mode, pass value of Stm Index out to Stm Index to continue executing the script from the position it was suspended unless you intend to change script flow. By default, Stm Index is equal to zero.
Run mode specifies a mode to execute a script. The VI provides modes described below. In Execute mode, the VI executes a script completely with no debugging features provided. Debugging modes specify conditions to suspend script execution and return. Debugging modes have line mode modification marked (LM). When line mode, the VI considers a set of statements starting in the same line as a single statement.

0ExecuteIt is a regular mode to execute a script. The VI starts executing a script from the position specified by Stm Index and runs until either the script is completed or an error occurs. It's default valiue.
1Abortterminates script execution and produces an error.
2RunThe VI starts executing a script from the position specified by Stm Index and runs until one of the conditions is met: a breakpoint is achieved, the script is completed, or an error occurs.
3StepThe VI executes a single statement.
4Step OverIf the current statement begins a syntax node (e.g. if, for, while), the VI executes all the statements of the node (and nested nodes, if any), and stops on the statement immediately following it. The VI stops within the node if a breakpoint is achieved.
5Step OutThe VI runs until it leaves a current syntax node (e.g. body of if, for, while), and stops on the statement immediately following it. The VI stops within the node if a breakpoint is achieved.
6Run (LM)It's line mode modification of Run.
7Step (LM)It's line mode modification of Step.
8Step Over (LM)It's line mode modification of Step Over.
9Step Out (LM)It's line mode modification of Step Out.
10unsupportedJust a stub value.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
exec parameters specifies optional parameters that affect execution of a script
pause counter is the maximum number of statements the VI can complete before yielding execution control. Larger values increase script execution speed, while smaller values improve the responsiveness and execution rate of other VIs in the running thread. By default, pause counter is equal to 1000.
pause, ms defines the number of milliseconds the VI is suspended after it executes the pause counter statements. If this parameter is greater than or equal to zero, the VI uses it as an input value for the Wait (ms) primitive. By default, pause, ms is equal to zero.
autoVar enables (TRUE) or disables (FALSE) automatic (implicit) creating variables. If a left-hand operand in an Assignment operator is an identifier that does not refer to an existing variable, CalcExpress creates a variable with the such name to perform an assignment if only autoVar is TRUE; otherwise an error is produced. Note that variables are created in a local variable context specified by VC Handle. By default, autoVar is TRUE.
enCpx enables (TRUE) or disables (FALSE) performing operators on operands of Complex data types (suppress polymorphism feature). By default, enCpx is TRUE.
Breakpoints specifies an array of statement indexes considered as breakpoints. The VI stops if any of the specified breakpoints is achieved while the VI is executing the script in a debugging mode.
return value is a value of expression in the return statement. If a script finished without the return statement, return value is zero.
dup CSE RefNum is a flow-through parameter with the same value as CSE RefNum.
Stm Index out returns an index of the statement to be executed next. If either the script is completed or an error occurred, Stm Index out returns -1.
Stop Reason returns a reason of the VI stop. The VI can only return Action completed and Pause to breath values, all the other values are reserved for compatibility with CSE Callback VIs.

0Exec StartIt's reserved for CSE Callback VI.
1Action completedIt's a typical termination status. If Stm Index out is less than zero, the VI finished script execution; herewith, a completion status is indicated in error out. If Stm Index out is equal to or greater than zero, the VI either performed the operation specified in Run mode, or achieved a specified breakpoint.
2pause to breathThe VI has not completed the required operation but suspended script execution because it completed number of statements specified in pause counter parameter of exec parameters cluster.
3reserved 1Reserved.
4reserved 2Reserved.
5customNot used.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.

 

CSE - Execute Script (Basic).vi - details

The VI is the basic CSE script executor. It can be used as is to execute scripts. As well, you can use it to create a custom script engine.

If Run mode is equal to zero (Execute), the VI completely executes a script starting from Stm Index position (statement) in a regular mode (debugging feature is off). Otherwise, the VI stops if either specified action is completed or a breakpoint is achieved.
